local_facts.claim: Texas Department of Insurance says an insurer generally has 15 business days to acknowledge a claim and, after receiving the information it needs, 15 business days to accept or reject it; an extension may apply in some circumstances.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A dated inspection report with clear roof photos gives an Austin homeowner a record to keep with the claim file. It documents roof conditions before or alongside an insurer's own adjuster inspection, without promising a coverage outcome.
local_facts.title: A roof record belongs in the Texas claim timeline

local_facts.claim: Austin Development Services lists Residential Express Building Permit triggers for roof repairs replacing decking boards over 128 square feet, or for more than 50% roofing replacement on a property in the Wildland-Urban Interface Code Area.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A roof inspection can identify damage and define a repair scope, but the scope may also require City review. Some asphalt-shingle work without structural effect may be exempt, while WUI properties can have additional roof-material requirements.
local_facts.title: Austin roof scope can change the permit path

local_facts.claim: The City of Austin reports 41% citywide tree canopy cover in 2022, measured from summer satellite imagery.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Mature canopy makes it important to document roof areas under branches and shade. An inspection can identify roof contact, debris accumulation, and the condition of shaded roof planes instead of attributing every issue generally to trees.
local_facts.title: Tree cover makes roof-area documentation more specific
